description: Block definitions for generate-blocks.sh. Each block produces a standalone HTML file.

blocks.name: Parallel Coords + Sparkline Table
blocks.prompt:
Build a parallel coordinates plot with a sparkline summary table below.

DATA: Generate 150 rows of synthetic city metrics with columns: city (string), population (10K-10M), avg_temp (30-90°F), elevation (0-8000ft), rainfall (5-80in), gdp_per_capita (15K-90K), density (50-25000/sq mi). Use realistic correlations (e.g., high elevation = lower temp).

UPPER PANEL — Parallel Coordinates:
- Canvas rendering for the polylines (150 lines with 0.4 opacity).
- SVG overlay for 6 vertical axes with labeled ticks.
- Intersection brushing: click-drag on any axis creates a brush filter. Lines outside the brush fade to 0.05 opacity.
- Multiple axes can be brushed simultaneously (intersection filtering).
- Tol bright palette: color lines by a categorical region column (6 regions).

LOWER PANEL — Summary Table:
- Shows one row per axis (6 rows).
- Columns: Axis Name, Sparkline (distribution of brushed subset, 60px wide), Min, Median, Max.
- Sparklines are tiny area charts drawn with inline SVG.
- Table updates live as brushes change.
- Show a count badge: "Showing N of 150 cities".

LAYOUT: Full viewport width, parallel coords takes top 55%, table takes bottom 35%, 10% for header/controls.

Remember: output raw HTML only, starting with <!DOCTYPE html>.

blocks.name: Linked Scatterplot Matrix
blocks.prompt:
Build a 4x4 scatterplot matrix (SPLOM) with linked brushing.

DATA: Generate 200 rows of synthetic iris-like data with 4 numeric columns (sepal_length 4-8, sepal_width 2-4.5, petal_length 1-7, petal_width 0.1-2.5) and a species column (3 categories). Make species clusters realistic.

SPLOM:
- 4x4 grid of scatterplots. Each cell is ~160x160px.
- Off-diagonal cells: scatterplots with 4px circles at 0.6 opacity.
- Diagonal cells: KDE density curves for each species overlaid (3 curves per cell).
- Color by species using Tol bright palette (3 colors).
- Column labels along the top and left.

BRUSHING:
- d3.brush on each off-diagonal cell.
- Brushing any cell highlights the same points in ALL other cells.
- Unhighlighted points fade to 0.1 opacity.
- Brush is removable by clicking outside.

Use d3.dispatch for cross-cell communication. SVG rendering is fine for 200 points.

Remember: output raw HTML only, starting with <!DOCTYPE html>.

blocks.name: Violin Plot Orchestra
blocks.prompt:
Build a ridgeline/violin hybrid showing temperature distributions.

DATA: Generate daily temperature data for 6 cities across 12 months. Each city-month has ~30 values drawn from a normal distribution with city-specific mean and seasonal variation. Cities: Oslo (cold), London (mild), Rome (warm), Cairo (hot), Mumbai (tropical), Singapore (equatorial).

LAYOUT:
- 12 columns (months) x 6 rows (cities).
- Each cell shows a split violin: left half is decade 2010-2019, right half is 2020-2029 (slightly warmer).
- Violins rendered as mirrored area paths from KDE (Epanechnikov kernel, bandwidth ~2).
- Shared y-scale across all cells (temperature 0-120°F).
- Color left half in cool blue (#4477AA), right half in warm orange (#EE6677).

LEGEND: Small legend at top showing "2010s" vs "2020s" with color swatches.
AXES: Month labels across top, city names on left, temperature scale on far left.
RESPONSIVE: Use viewBox for scaling. Minimum readable at 600px width.

Remember: output raw HTML only, starting with <!DOCTYPE html>.

blocks.name: Bee Swarm Census
blocks.prompt:
Build a bee swarm plot of 400 synthetic people by income, with annotation callouts.

DATA: Generate 400 records with income (log-normal distribution, median ~55K, range 15K-500K), education_level (4 categories: High School, Bachelor's, Master's, PhD — correlated with income), and age (22-65).

BEE SWARM:
- Horizontal layout: x-axis is income (log scale), y-axis is jittered using d3.forceY(0) + d3.forceCollide(3.5) to prevent overlap.
- Circles are 3px radius, colored by education_level (4 Tol bright colors).
- Run force simulation to convergence (alpha < 0.01) before rendering.

ANNOTATIONS:
- Vertical dashed lines at 25th, 50th, 75th percentiles with labels.
- Callout annotations for the 3 highest earners: leader line from the dot to a text label showing "$XXXk, PhD, age YY".
- A side box plot (right margin) summarizing the overall distribution: whiskers at 5th/95th, box at Q1/Q3, line at median.

LEGEND: Color legend for education levels at top-right.

Remember: output raw HTML only, starting with <!DOCTYPE html>.

blocks.name: Crossfilter Flight Explorer
blocks.prompt:
Build a crossfilter-style explorer with 3 linked histogram views.

DATA: Generate 2000 synthetic flight records with: departure_hour (0-23, peak at 8 and 17), delay_minutes (-10 to 180, right-skewed), distance_miles (100-3000), carrier (6 airlines), day_of_week (0-6).

THREE PANELS (stacked vertically, each ~200px tall):
1. DEPARTURE HOUR histogram (24 bars, one per hour)
2. DELAY histogram (20 bins from -10 to 180 minutes)
3. DISTANCE histogram (15 bins from 100 to 3000 miles)

CROSSFILTER BEHAVIOR:
- Each panel has a d3.brushX.
- Brushing one panel filters the data shown in the OTHER two panels.
- Multiple brushes can be active simultaneously (intersection logic).
- Implement with simple array filtering (no crossfilter library needed).
- Bars shrink/grow with smooth 300ms transitions.
- Active (filtered-in) bars in Tol blue (#4477AA), background (total) bars in light gray.

COUNTER: Top of page shows "Showing N of 2,000 flights" that updates live.
CLEAR: A "Reset All" button that clears all brushes.

Remember: output raw HTML only, starting with <!DOCTYPE html>.

blocks.name: QQ Plot with Confidence Bands
blocks.prompt:
Build a normal QQ plot with confidence envelope and histogram inset.

DATA: Generate 200 synthetic values from a slightly skewed distribution (mix of 80% normal(50,10) + 20% normal(75,5)) to make the QQ plot interesting — it should deviate from normality in the tails.

MAIN CHART — QQ Plot (500x500px):
- X-axis: theoretical quantiles (standard normal).
- Y-axis: sample quantiles.
- Points: 200 circles, 4px radius, Tol blue (#4477AA), 0.7 opacity.
- Reference line: 45-degree line (through Q1 and Q3) in dark gray, dashed.
- 95% confidence envelope: shaded band around the reference line using ±1.96 * SE formula. Fill with light blue at 0.2 opacity.
- Points outside the envelope highlighted in Tol red (#EE6677).

INSET — Histogram (150x100px, positioned top-left corner):
- Small histogram of the raw data with ~20 bins.
- Overlaid normal curve (fitted mean and SD).
- Subtle gray styling so it doesn't dominate.

ANNOTATIONS:
- Text annotation pointing to the right tail: "Right tail deviates — mixture component".
- Axis labels: "Theoretical Quantiles" and "Sample Quantiles".
- Title: "Normal QQ Plot — Testing for Normality".

TOOLTIP: Hover a point to see its value and z-score.

Remember: output raw HTML only, starting with <!DOCTYPE html>.

blocks.name: Density Contour Heatmap
blocks.prompt:
Build a 2D density visualization with contours and raw points.

DATA: Generate 8,000 2D points from 3 bivariate normal clusters with different means and covariances. Cluster 1: center (0.3, 0.4), N=4000. Cluster 2: center (0.7, 0.7), N=2500. Cluster 3: center (0.2, 0.8), N=1500.

LAYERS (bottom to top):
1. CANVAS layer: Raw points as 1.5px dots with 0.15 opacity, colored by nearest cluster center.
2. SVG layer: d3.contourDensity contour lines (10 threshold levels). Use a sequential blue-to-red color scale for contour fills at 0.3 opacity. Contour lines in dark gray, 0.5px stroke.

INTERACTION:
- d3.brush on the SVG layer. Brush a rectangle to zoom into that region.
- Double-click to reset zoom.
- Smooth zoom transition (750ms).
- Contours recompute after zoom to show local density detail.

AXES: X and Y axes with ticks. Labels "Feature 1" and "Feature 2".
LEGEND: Color ramp legend for density levels.
SIZE: Full viewport width, 600px height.

Remember: output raw HTML only, starting with <!DOCTYPE html>.

blocks.name: Small Multiples Seasonal
blocks.prompt:
Build a 12-panel small multiples chart showing daily energy consumption by month.

DATA: Generate 3 years (2022-2024) of daily energy consumption (kWh). Pattern: winter high (~45 kWh), summer high (~40 kWh, AC), spring/fall low (~25 kWh). Add day-of-week pattern (weekends lower) and random noise.

LAYOUT: 4 columns x 3 rows grid. Each panel is one month (Jan-Dec).

EACH PANEL:
- X-axis: day of month (1-31).
- Y-axis: shared across all panels (0-60 kWh).
- Three overlaid line/area layers, one per year: 2022 (light), 2023 (medium), 2024 (dark).
- Use Tol sequential blues for the 3 years.
- Area fill at 0.15 opacity under each line.
- Month name as panel title.

INTERACTION:
- Vertical hover crosshair that syncs across ALL 12 panels.
- On hover, show the day and all 3 years' values in a tooltip near the cursor.
- Use pointer events on a transparent overlay rect per panel.

SHARED AXIS: Single y-axis label on the far left. Single x-axis label at the bottom.
RESPONSIVE: viewBox-based. Panels reflow to 3x4 at narrow widths (via CSS grid + SVG viewBox per panel).

Remember: output raw HTML only, starting with <!DOCTYPE html>.

blocks.name: Sparkline Dashboard Table
blocks.prompt:
Build a sortable data table with embedded sparkline charts in every row.

DATA: Generate 25 rows of synthetic stock data. Each row: ticker (3-4 letter code), company_name, sector (5 sectors), price (current, 10-500), prices_30d (array of 30 daily prices), volume_7d (array of 7 daily volumes), daily_returns_20d (array of 20 daily returns, positive or negative), performance_pct (-30 to +50), target_pct (performance target).

TABLE COLUMNS:
1. Ticker (text, bold)
2. Sector (text, colored dot prefix using Tol bright, one color per sector)
3. 30-Day Price (sparkline: 60px wide area chart with last-value dot)
4. Volume (spark bar chart: 7 bars, 40px wide, gray)
5. Win/Loss (20-day strip: 20 tiny rects, green for positive return, red for negative)
6. Performance (bullet chart: 80px wide, gray bar = target, colored bar = actual, green if exceeds target, red if below)
7. Price (right-aligned number, formatted with $ and commas)

SORTING: Click any column header to sort ascending/descending. Arrow indicator on active sort column. Rows animate to new positions (300ms transition on transform).

STYLING: Alternating row backgrounds. Sticky header. Compact font (12px). Monospace for numbers.

Remember: output raw HTML only, starting with <!DOCTYPE html>.

blocks.name: Strip Plot with Marginals
blocks.prompt:
Build a scatterplot with marginal strip plots and regression line.

DATA: Generate 250 points with x (age, 20-70) and y (cholesterol, 150-300), positively correlated (r ≈ 0.55). Add a group column (3 categories: Low Risk, Medium Risk, High Risk) correlated with both variables.

CENTER — Scatterplot (500x400px):
- 250 circles, 4px radius, colored by group (Tol bright, 3 colors), 0.6 opacity.
- Regression line with equation annotation: "y = mx + b, R² = 0.XX".
- Regression line dashed, dark gray.

TOP MARGIN — X Strip Plot (500x40px):
- Jittered strip plot of x values. Same colors as center.
- Tiny box plot overlay (whiskers + box + median line).

RIGHT MARGIN — Y Strip Plot (40x400px):
- Same as top, but vertical for y values.

BRUSHING:
- d3.brush on the center scatterplot.
- Brushed points are highlighted; marginal strips filter to show only brushed points.
- Box plot summaries in margins update to reflect the brushed subset.

AXES: "Age (years)" on x, "Cholesterol (mg/dL)" on y.
LEGEND: Top-right, showing 3 risk groups.

Remember: output raw HTML only, starting with <!DOCTYPE html>.

blocks.name: Zoomable Treemap
blocks.prompt:
Build a zoomable treemap with breadcrumb navigation.

DATA: Generate a 3-level hierarchy of synthetic file system data. Root has 8 top-level directories (Documents, Photos, Code, Music, Videos, Downloads, Projects, Archives). Each has 3-6 subdirectories. Each subdirectory has 5-15 files with size (1KB to 500MB, log-distributed). Total ~400 leaf nodes.

TREEMAP:
- Full viewport width, 600px height.
- d3.treemapSquarify tiling.
- Color by top-level directory (8 colors from Tol bright + Tol muted).
- Leaf labels shown when cell > 40px in both dimensions. Truncate with ellipsis.
- Cell borders: 1px white.

ZOOM INTERACTION:
- Click a non-leaf cell to zoom into it (fills the viewport with that subtree).
- Smooth 750ms transition: cells grow/shrink/reposition.
- Breadcrumb bar at top: "Root > Documents > Work" — click any segment to zoom to that level.
- Click a leaf cell to show a tooltip with full path and size.

HEADER: Title "File System Explorer" with total size.
LEGEND: Color legend for top-level directories.

Remember: output raw HTML only, starting with <!DOCTYPE html>.

blocks.name: Sunburst to Icicle Morph
blocks.prompt:
Build a hierarchy visualization that morphs between sunburst and icicle layouts.

DATA: Generate a 3-level organizational hierarchy. Root company has 5 departments, each with 3-5 teams, each with 4-10 members. ~150 leaf nodes. Each leaf has a value (salary, 40K-200K).

SUNBURST VIEW:
- Centered, 500px diameter.
- d3.partition with .size([2 * Math.PI, radius]).
- Arcs colored by department (5 Tol bright colors), saturation decreasing with depth.
- Labels on arcs that are wide enough (> 12px).

ICICLE VIEW:
- Full width, 400px height.
- d3.partition with .size([width, height]).
- Rectangles with same coloring scheme.
- Labels in rectangles that are wide enough.

MORPH BUTTON:
- A toggle button: "Switch to Icicle" / "Switch to Sunburst".
- On click, smoothly interpolate between arc and rect over 1200ms.
- For sunburst→icicle: interpolate startAngle/endAngle to x/width and innerRadius/outerRadius to y/height.
- Use d3.interpolate on the layout coordinates, render with a custom tween.

HOVER: Highlight the hovered node and its ancestors. Show path and value in a tooltip.

Remember: output raw HTML only, starting with <!DOCTYPE html>.

blocks.name: Radial Dendrogram + Edge Bundling
blocks.prompt:
Build a radial dendrogram with hierarchical edge bundling.

DATA: Generate a software package dependency tree. Root package has 6 modules. Each module has 4-8 submodules. Each submodule has 2-5 files. Total ~120 leaf nodes. Generate ~80 cross-module dependency edges (imports between files in different modules).

LAYOUT:
- d3.cluster in radial layout, 600px diameter.
- Leaf nodes arranged around the circle perimeter.
- Module names as labels rotated to follow the circle.

EDGE BUNDLING (Canvas layer):
- Dependencies rendered as hierarchically bundled curves on Canvas.
- Use LCA (Lowest Common Ancestor) path routing.
- d3.curveBundle.beta(tension) for the curves.
- Default tension: 0.85.
- Edge color: light gray (#999) at 0.3 opacity.

TENSION SLIDER:
- Range input (0 to 1, step 0.05) controlling bundle tension.
- At 0: straight lines between nodes. At 1: tight bundling along the hierarchy.
- Canvas redraws on slider change.

HOVER INTERACTION:
- Hover a leaf node: highlight all its direct dependency edges in Tol blue (#4477AA) at full opacity. Fade all other edges to 0.05.
- Highlight the hovered node and its dependency targets with larger dots.

SVG layer: node labels and hover targets. Canvas layer: all edges.

Remember: output raw HTML only, starting with <!DOCTYPE html>.

blocks.name: Force-Directed Clustering
blocks.prompt:
Build a force-directed network with 400 nodes in 7 clusters.

DATA: Generate 400 nodes assigned to 7 clusters (sizes: 80, 70, 60, 55, 50, 45, 40). Generate ~600 edges: 80% within-cluster (dense), 20% between-cluster (sparse). Each node has a size value (1-5).

FORCE SIMULATION:
- d3.forceSimulation with:
  - forceLink: edges with distance 30 (within-cluster) or 80 (between-cluster).
  - forceManyBody: strength -20.
  - forceX/forceY: pull toward cluster centroid positions (arrange 7 centroids in a circle).
  - forceCollide: radius based on node size * 2 + 1.
- Run simulation. Let it animate from initial random positions.

RENDERING:
- Canvas for all nodes and edges (performance).
- Edges: 0.15 opacity gray lines.
- Nodes: circles colored by cluster (7 Tol bright + muted colors), sized by value (2-6px radius).
- Cluster labels: SVG text at each cluster centroid.

INTERACTION:
- Drag nodes with d3.drag (reheat simulation on drag).
- Hover node: highlight it and its neighbors, show degree in a tooltip.
- Canvas hit detection via d3.quadtree for nearest node lookup on mousemove.

Remember: output raw HTML only, starting with <!DOCTYPE html>.

blocks.name: Adjacency Matrix Reorder
blocks.prompt:
Build a 35x35 adjacency matrix with reorderable rows and columns.

DATA: Generate 35 nodes in 5 communities (7 per community). Create ~200 edges: dense within-community, sparse between. Edge weight 1-5.

MATRIX (500x500px):
- 35x35 grid of cells. Cell color = edge weight (sequential blue scale, 0 = white).
- Row and column labels (node names like "A1"-"A7", "B1"-"B7", etc.).
- Diagonal cells in light yellow.

REORDERING:
- Three buttons: "By Name" (alphabetical), "By Degree" (highest degree first), "By Community" (group communities together).
- On click, rows AND columns reorder simultaneously with a 750ms transition.
- Cells slide to new positions (transition on x and y).

HOVER:
- Hover a cell: highlight entire row and column with a subtle background.
- Show tooltip: "A3 → B5: weight 3".

SIDE BAR CHART (right margin, 100px wide):
- Horizontal bar for each node showing its degree.
- Bars reorder with the matrix.
- Colored by community.

LEGEND: Color scale legend for edge weight. Community color legend.

Remember: output raw HTML only, starting with <!DOCTYPE html>.

blocks.name: Sankey Energy Flow
blocks.prompt:
Build a Sankey diagram showing energy production to consumption flow.

DATA: Synthetic energy flow with 5 stages:
1. Sources: Coal, Natural Gas, Nuclear, Solar, Wind, Hydro
2. Generation: Thermal, Renewable
3. Grid: Transmission, Distribution
4. Sectors: Residential, Commercial, Industrial, Transport
5. End Use: Heating, Cooling, Lighting, Motors, Electronics, Transport

Generate ~35 links with realistic flow values (total ~1000 units). Include some loss links (Transmission Loss, Distribution Loss).

SANKEY:
- d3.sankey() layout. Full viewport width, 500px height.
- Nodes: rectangles, colored by stage (5 colors from Tol bright).
- Links: gradient fill from source to target color. 0.4 opacity.
- Node labels positioned outside (left for first stage, right for last).
- Link labels: show value on hover.

INTERACTION:
- Drag nodes vertically to reposition.
- Hover a node: highlight all connected links (increase opacity to 0.8), fade others.
- Hover a link: tooltip showing "Source → Target: XX units (YY%)".

ANNOTATIONS:
- Total energy label at the top.
- Loss flows colored in red (#CC3311) with "Loss" labels.

RESPONSIVE: viewBox-based scaling.

Remember: output raw HTML only, starting with <!DOCTYPE html>.

blocks.name: Chord Diagram of Trade
blocks.prompt:
Build a chord diagram showing trade flows between 10 countries.

DATA: Generate a 10x10 trade matrix (in billions USD) for: USA, China, Germany, Japan, UK, France, South Korea, India, Canada, Mexico. Make values realistic (USA-China ~600B, USA-Canada ~400B, etc.). Matrix is asymmetric (imports ≠ exports).

CHORD DIAGRAM:
- d3.chord() layout, 550px diameter, centered.
- Outer arcs: one per country, colored with Tol bright palette (10 colors).
- Chords: colored by the larger exporter in the pair, 0.5 opacity.
- Arc labels: country names positioned outside the arcs.
- Tick marks on arcs every $100B with labels every $500B.

ENTRANCE ANIMATION:
- On load, chords grow from zero width to final size over 1200ms.
- Arcs grow from zero angle to final angle.
- Staggered: arcs first (400ms), then chords (800ms).
- Use d3.transition with d3.easeCubicOut.

HOVER:
- Hover a country arc: fade all chords not connected to that country to 0.05 opacity.
- Show a tooltip: "USA: $X.XB exports, $X.XB imports, $X.XB total trade".
- Hover a chord: tooltip showing bilateral trade values.

Remember: output raw HTML only, starting with <!DOCTYPE html>.

blocks.name: Collapsible Tree with Search
blocks.prompt:
Build a collapsible tree with a search box that highlights matches.

DATA: Generate a biological taxonomy tree. Root "Life" has 4 domains, each with 2-4 kingdoms, each with 3-5 phyla, each with 2-4 classes, some with 2-3 orders. Total ~200 nodes, 5 levels deep. Use real-ish names (Animalia, Chordata, Mammalia, etc.).

TREE:
- d3.tree layout, horizontal (root on left).
- Initially: expand first 2 levels, collapse deeper nodes.
- Collapsed nodes show a small "+" indicator and a count badge "(N descendants)".
- Click a node to expand/collapse with smooth 500ms transition.
- Links: curved (d3.linkHorizontal), gray 1px.
- Nodes: 6px circles. Leaf nodes filled, internal nodes hollow.

SEARCH:
- Text input at top: "Search taxonomy..."
- As user types, find all nodes whose name matches (case-insensitive substring).
- Auto-expand the paths from root to all matching nodes.
- Matching nodes highlighted in Tol red (#EE6677) with a glow effect.
- Non-matching visible nodes at 0.3 opacity.
- Clear the search to restore normal view.

SIZING: The tree scrolls horizontally if wider than viewport. Use a container with overflow-x: auto. Height adapts to expanded node count.

Remember: output raw HTML only, starting with <!DOCTYPE html>.

blocks.name: Circle Packing Zoom
blocks.prompt:
Build a zoomable circle packing layout.

DATA: Generate a hierarchy of synthetic Wikipedia categories. Root has 6 top categories (Science, Arts, History, Technology, Geography, Sports). Each has 4-6 subcategories. Each subcategory has 5-12 articles with a value (article length, 500-50000 words). Total ~300 leaf nodes.

CIRCLE PACKING:
- d3.pack layout. 700px diameter, centered.
- Circles colored by top-level category (6 Tol bright colors), with decreasing saturation at deeper levels.
- Leaf circles filled with light tint, internal circles with stroke only.
- Labels: show on circles with radius > 20px. Font size proportional to circle radius.

ZOOM:
- Click any internal circle to zoom into it. The clicked circle fills the viewport.
- Smooth 750ms zoom transition using d3.interpolateZoom.
- Labels appear/disappear based on whether they'd be readable at current zoom level (LOD).
- Click the background or the current root circle to zoom out one level.

TOOLTIP: Hover a leaf to see article name and word count.
BREADCRUMB: Path display at top: "Wikipedia > Science > Physics > Quantum Mechanics".

Remember: output raw HTML only, starting with <!DOCTYPE html>.

blocks.name: Arc Diagram
blocks.prompt:
Build an arc diagram showing character co-occurrences in a synthetic novel.

DATA: Generate 30 characters with names, chapter_first_appearance (1-25), and importance (1-10). Generate ~80 co-occurrence edges with weights (1-20). Characters who appear in similar chapters have higher co-occurrence.

ARC DIAGRAM:
- Horizontal layout, full viewport width.
- X-axis: characters positioned by first_appearance (left=early, right=late). Use d3.scaleLinear.
- Nodes: circles on the x-axis baseline, sized by importance (3-10px radius).
- Arcs: semicircular curves above the baseline connecting co-occurring characters.
- Arc height proportional to weight (higher = taller arc).
- Arc color: Tol bright palette based on the earlier character's first chapter (sequential scale).
- Arc stroke width: 1-3px based on weight.
- Arc opacity: 0.4.

INTERACTION:
- Hover a node: highlight all its arcs at full opacity, show character name and degree.
- Fade non-connected arcs to 0.05.

BRUSH:
- d3.brushX on the x-axis to select a chapter range.
- Only show arcs where BOTH endpoints are within the brushed range.
- Update a label: "Chapters X-Y: N connections".

Node labels shown for characters with importance > 7.

Remember: output raw HTML only, starting with <!DOCTYPE html>.

blocks.name: US Choropleth
blocks.prompt:
Build a US state choropleth map with tooltips and a color legend.

DATA: Generate synthetic data for all 50 US states + DC: state_name, state_fips, value (a metric like "broadband access %" ranging 60-98%), and a category.

MAP:
- Use d3.geoAlbersUsa projection.
- Embed a simplified US states TopoJSON inline (you can use the standard us-atlas topojson — include it as a JS object literal with state boundaries). If that's too large, generate simplified polygon coordinates for all 50 states + DC that approximate their shapes.
- States filled by value using a sequential blue color scale (d3.interpolateBlues).
- State borders: 0.5px white stroke.
- Alaska and Hawaii repositioned by the AlbersUsa projection.

INTERACTION:
- Hover a state: darken its fill, show tooltip with state name and value.
- Click a state: zoom to it (smooth 750ms transition using d3.zoom transform). Click background to reset.

LEGEND:
- Horizontal color bar legend at bottom with labeled threshold breaks.
- 5 discrete color steps with values.

TITLE: "Broadband Access by State (%)".
RESPONSIVE: viewBox-based.

Note: Since this must be self-contained with no external fetches, generate approximate state path data inline or use a very simplified TopoJSON. Prioritize having all 50 states recognizable over geometric precision.

Remember: output raw HTML only, starting with <!DOCTYPE html>.

blocks.name: Rotating Globe
blocks.prompt:
Build an interactive rotating globe with pulsing city points.

GEOMETRY: Embed simplified world country outlines as GeoJSON inline (use very simplified polygons — major countries recognizable but low vertex count, ~30 countries is fine). Or generate approximate coastline polygons.

GLOBE (Canvas, 600x600):
- d3.geoOrthographic projection, centered.
- Canvas multi-layer: Layer 1 = ocean (dark blue fill), Layer 2 = land (light fill with stroke), Layer 3 = graticule (thin gray lines every 15°), Layer 4 = cities.
- Auto-rotate: gentle rotation (0.3°/frame) around the y-axis when not interacting.

CITY POINTS:
- 30 major world cities with [lon, lat] coordinates (hardcoded: NYC, London, Tokyo, Sydney, etc.).
- Render as circles on the globe surface (visible only on the front hemisphere).
- Pulsing animation: radius oscillates between 2px and 5px using sin(time).
- Color by continent (6 colors from Tol bright).

INTERACTION:
- Click-drag to rotate the globe (versor-based rotation for natural feel).
- On drag start, stop auto-rotation. Resume auto-rotation 3 seconds after drag ends.
- Hover near a city (within 10px): show city name as a label.

DRAW TERMINATOR: A day/night line (great circle) based on a simulated sun position.

Remember: output raw HTML only, starting with <!DOCTYPE html>.

blocks.name: Hex Bin Map
blocks.prompt:
Build a hex-binned map of the US showing point density.

DATA: Generate 20,000 synthetic GPS-like points concentrated around US population centers (NYC, LA, Chicago, Houston, Phoenix, etc. — use 15 city centers with different weights). Points follow 2D normal distributions around each center.

MAP LAYERS:
1. Canvas layer: hex bins using d3.hexbin. Hex radius = 8px. Color by count using a sequential orange scale (d3.interpolateOranges). Draw hexagons as filled paths on Canvas.
2. SVG overlay: simplified US state outlines (thin gray stroke, no fill). Use d3.geoAlbersUsa.

LEGEND: Color ramp legend showing point count per hex.

INTERACTION:
- Hover a hex: show tooltip with count and approximate location.
- Use quadtree or pixel-based hit detection on Canvas for the hex hover.

CONTROLS:
- Slider for hex radius (4-16px). Recompute hexbin on change.
- The map re-renders with the new hex size.

SIZING: Full viewport width, aspect ratio matching AlbersUsa (~960x600).

Note: Embed simplified US state boundaries inline as a JS array of [lon,lat] polygons. They don't need to be perfect — recognizable outlines are sufficient.

Remember: output raw HTML only, starting with <!DOCTYPE html>.

blocks.name: Flow Map with Curved Arrows
blocks.prompt:
Build a map showing animated migration flows between US cities.

DATA: 12 major US cities with [lon, lat]: NYC, LA, Chicago, Houston, Phoenix, Philadelphia, San Antonio, San Diego, Dallas, Seattle, Denver, Miami. Generate 25 directed migration flows with volume (1000-50000 people).

MAP:
- d3.geoAlbersUsa projection.
- Light gray US outline as background (simplified inline paths).

blocks.prompt:
Build a generative phyllotaxis (sunflower spiral) animation.

PHYLLOTAXIS:
- 2000 dots arranged in a sunflower spiral.
- Position: for dot i, angle = i * goldenAngle, radius = sqrt(i) * spacing.
- Golden angle ≈ 137.508°.

CANVAS RENDERING (centered, 700x700, dark background #111):
- Each dot: circle with radius 2-5px (larger toward the outside).
- Color: HSL with hue cycling based on angle (hue = angle % 360), saturation 70%, lightness 55%.
- This creates a rainbow spiral pattern.

ANIMATION (d3.timer):
- Slowly vary the angle parameter: goldenAngle + sin(time/5000) * 0.02.
- This tiny variation causes the entire pattern to shift between spiral arms — mesmerizing.
- Also slowly rotate the entire pattern: each dot's angle += time * 0.0001.
- Pulsing: each dot's radius oscillates with sin(time/1000 + i * 0.01) * 1.5.

BLOOM EFFECT:
- Draw each dot twice: once at normal size with full opacity, once at 3x size with 0.1 opacity for a glow.
- Use globalCompositeOperation = 'lighter' for the glow pass to create additive blending.

CONTROLS:
- Slider: "Dots" (500-3000, default 2000).
- Slider: "Angle Offset" (0-0.1, controls the variation amplitude).
- Slider: "Speed" (0.1-3, multiplier on animation speed).
- Pause/Play button.

The overall effect should look like a living, breathing mathematical flower.

Remember: output raw HTML only, starting with <!DOCTYPE html>.
